itens.det: 1999 JP Comm. Evolution Campaign - Masaki Promo Holo
itens.about: Distributed in Japan through the 1999 Evolution Campaign, a promotion where players who brought an evolved Pokemon to participating stores received a holo promo card. These early Japanese promos used a simpler, glossier foil pattern than the retail set holos of the same era, which is part of why clean, gem-quality copies are hard to find today.

itens.about: The Base Set Charizard is the single most recognized card in the hobby: the flagship holo of the original 1999 English print run, made instantly famous by its stage-2 Fire-type power and the small '1st Edition' stamp on early copies. It effectively created the modern graded-card market and remains the reference point every other chase card is compared against.

itens.det: 1998 JP CoroCoro Comics Prize - Pokemon Illustrator Promo
itens.about: The single most famous Pokemon card in existence. Awarded only to the top winners of CoroCoro Comics illustration contests between 1997 and 1999, it was never sold or included in any set — an estimated 39 copies exist worldwide, none of them Pokemon cards in the traditional sense but rather certificates honoring the winning artist. It has repeatedly set the record for the most expensive trading card ever sold.
itens.graderInfo: TAG (Technical Authentication & Grading) is a newer entrant in card grading, built around computer-vision analysis and a public QR-code lookup that shows the exact photos used to grade each card — the DIG Report referenced by the certificate number on this listing.

Its H-series holos used a rare 'Crystal' style foil made only for this set, and because Skyridge had a short print run before the license changed hands, its top holos are some of the scarcer pulls from the WOTC era.

itens.det: 2006 EX Holon Phantoms #104/110 - Gold Star Holo
itens.about: Gold Star cards were a short-lived rarity tier (2003-2006) inserted at a far lower rate than regular holos, identifiable by the gold star next to the Pokemon's name and slightly altered artwork. Holon Phantoms was one of the last sets to feature them before the mechanic was retired, which is a major reason Gold Stars remain a benchmark chase for EX-era collectors.

itens.det: 2000 WOTC - Pokemon The Movie 2000 Promo Holo

Its full-art holo and untranslated runic text (a mix of medieval Futhark and Gothenburg runes) made it one of the most recognizable promos ever printed, even though it was never legal for tournament play.
